03What It IsOVERVIEW▶

Every one of Swami's own skills gets a skill sheet, a vibe-dashboard page in a fixed shape that explains what the skill is, how to use it on macOS and Windows, what it depends on, where it runs, and its gotchas. This skill makes those pages. Each one is rendered from a skill card, a JSON file holding the facts about the skill plus a fingerprint of its files.

The fingerprint is what keeps the pages honest: when any file in a skill changes, its fingerprint changes, so a later check (or the Skill Library's nightly refresh) can flag the page as out of date. Swami vets every page before it goes public. The skill only ever makes a private draft; nothing goes to GitHub until he says "publish" for that skill.

Why it mattersSwami shares his skills with other people, including Windows users. A skill sheet tells them what a skill does and what it needs before they install it, and the fingerprint means a stale page is caught instead of quietly drifting from the skill it describes.
04What It DoesOVERVIEW▶
  • CreateReads every file in the skill, fingerprints it, writes the card, builds the page, records the audio overview, checks it in a browser, and publishes a private draft artifact titled "<Title> skill".
  • UpdateRe-reads a skill that changed, updates only what the change affects (keeping Swami's edits and answers), and republishes the draft to the same link.
  • CheckCompares every card's fingerprint with the skill as it is now and replies with a table: fresh, out of date, no dashboard yet, or skill missing.
  • PublishAfter Swami's go, marks the card published and commits the page, card and narration to dashboards/<skill>/ in the public claude-skills repo, where GitHub Pages serves it.
  • Fixed SectionsEvery sheet has the same 16 sections in the same order, from Dashboard Summary and Search to Where It Runs, Gotchas, Card and Freshness, Mind Map, Glossary and the skill's own SKILL.md word for word.
  • Both SystemsEvery card covers macOS and Windows: Windows install notes for each program, Windows steps, and Windows gotchas and requirements.
  • Open QuestionsAnything it could not confirm from the skill's files goes in the card's confirm list and shows on the draft until Swami answers. A sheet can't be published while that list is open.
  • RegistryKeeps dashboards/index.json, the list of published sheets with their fingerprints, which the Skill Library reads every night to show each sheet's link and an out-of-date flag.
  • PrivacyRuns vibe-dashboard's privacy scan on the page, card and narration before every publish and commit, so no one under NDA is ever named.

08Capabilities and LimitationsSCOPE▶
  • Stays CurrentThe builder takes vibe-dashboard's patches from its current SKILL.md, so a rebuild picks up the latest Search, Mind Map and table-fit behavior.
  • Stale Pages FlaggedAny change to any file in a skill changes its fingerprint, so check mode and the Skill Library's nightly refresh both catch an out-of-date sheet.
  • Rebuildable DraftsEach draft carries its card and narration as published files, so a later session can rebuild it without starting over.
  • Skill LinksThe Skill Library's "How the Skills Connect" section reads each published card's skill dependencies, with the reason for each link.
  • Safe PublishingNothing goes public without Swami's "publish", and the privacy scan runs before every commit.
  • One At A TimeOne skill per run unless Swami asks for more.
  • Swami's Skills OnlyMade for Swami's own skills (Customize › Skills › Yours) and his repo; it does not document Anthropic's built-in skills.
  • No Refresh ButtonSkill sheets have no owner-only audio refresh button, because the public copy lives on GitHub Pages, where it can't work. Update mode re-records the audio instead.
  • Untested ClaimsIt never invents results: anything nobody has tried, such as a skill on Windows or in another AI, is marked Untested.
  • Sync LagAfter Swami uploads a changed skill, Claude's synced copy can lag by up to about half an hour, so a fresh fingerprint may still show the old version.

11GotchasGOTCHAS▶
  • Duplicate DraftsBefore creating a draft, check dashboards/index.json and the artifact list for one that already exists; a second draft of the same skill causes confusion about which to publish.
  • Braces In CardsCard text must not contain double curly braces: the builder treats them as unfilled template placeholders and stops.
  • Capturing GroupsGlossary match patterns must use non-capturing groups such as (?:es)?. A capturing group breaks the page's term matcher, so the build stops on one.
  • File PathsFiles published beside a draft must come from the scratchpad or working directory, or the publish is refused.
  • Checking Pagesgithub.io can be blocked from Claude's workspace, so check a published sheet through raw.githubusercontent.com instead.
  • Capability WarningPublishing a draft warns that the page uses mcp without declaring it. That's the audio player's unused refresh code; sheets declare no capabilities, so ignore it.
  • Stress MarksFix wrong noun or verb stress in the card's spoken block, not just the narration file, or the next rebuild brings the mistake back.
12Other RequirementsREFERENCE▶
  • GitHubClaude's GitHub access with push rights to swami-claude-skills/claude-skills, and GitHub Pages turned on for it.
  • CapabilitiesCode execution with network access (GitHub, and the voice model the first time), and artifacts.
  • MemorySwami's memory naming the people under NDA, for the privacy scan.
  • ComputerAny Mac (macOS) or Windows 10 or 11 PC with a browser, to vet drafts. Nothing is installed on it.
